ai.title: Simplify base2 agent orchestration prompts
ai.summary: Refactored `base2-factory.ts` system and instruction prompts to remove rigid step-by-step workflows. Replaced numbered phases with flexible conditional spawning logic for planner, editor, and reviewer. Removed explicit `stepPrompt` fallback in favor of autonomous iteration guidance. Covers internal agent definition configuration only.

eli5.text: The helper that runs the base2 coding agent no longer follows a fixed three-step script (plan, then edit, then review) and instead decides in the moment whether to bring in a planner, an editor, or a reviewer based on what the task needs. You wouldn't see a visible difference in how the agent talks or works today, but internally it has a bit more freedom to skip steps it deems unnecessary and to end its turn when it feels it has useful information rather than pushing through a required review. This is strictly behind-the-scenes configuration for how the internal agent orchestrates its sub-tasks, so nothing about your experience or access changes.

ai.title: Secure API keys, session hashing, CSRF, schema updates
ai.summary: Hardened API key and session endpoints with same-origin CSRF enforcement and SHA-256 session ID hashing. Database schema updated via migration 0025 to simplify session types to 'web', 'pat', and 'cli' with automated backfill logic. New crypto utilities and confirmation dialogs added to the UI layer to support secure identity verification and session management.

eli5.text: When you manage your login sessions or API keys in your web browser, the system now double-checks that any action you take (like revoking a key or logging out) actually came from our own app, making it harder for malicious sites to trick you. Your active sessions are now tracked as simpler, clearly labeled types (web browser, API token, or command-line tool), and the system automatically sorted your existing sessions into these new buckets so you don't lose access. You would notice that actions requiring confirmation now prompt you more explicitly before deleting something important, and your session list will appear cleaner with consistent, predictable labels. These security and cleanup changes were part of the update released today.

ai.title: Fix session type migration logic in 0025milkylilacheney.sql
ai.summary: Corrects SQL logic in migration 0025_milky_lila_cheney.sql to properly identify CLI sessions. The WHERE clause now requires fingerprint_id IS NOT NULL instead of IS NULL, ensuring sessions with valid fingerprints and far-future expiration are marked as 'cli'. This fix applies to the common/src/db/migrations directory.

eli5.text: When your account signs in through the terminal or command line, the system now correctly labels that session as a CLI session. Previously, it was looking for sessions that had no fingerprint and marking those as CLI, but now it correctly looks for sessions that do have a fingerprint and a far-future expiration. If you're someone who uses the system through terminal commands, your sessions will now be properly identified as CLI type sessions instead of being left unmarked or mislabeled.

ai.title: Unify session revocation via DELETE /api/sessions
ai.summary: Consolidated session and token revocation logic into a single `DELETE /api/sessions` endpoint, removing legacy per-id routes like `/api/api-keys/[id]` and `/api/user/sessions/[id]`. This refactor supports batch operations via `sessionIds` and `tokenIds` arrays while enforcing origin checks and distinguishing between web and PAT sessions. The security UI in `web/src/app/security/page.tsx` now uses tabs to separate web and CLI sessions, updating the client to use the new unified API.

eli5.text: The account security page now uses a single, simpler action to log you out of sessions or revoke access tokens, instead of handling each one separately through different hidden paths. When you sign in and visit the security settings, you'll see two tabs, one for web sessions (your open browser windows) and one for app tokens (programs accessing your account on your behalf), and you can now revoke multiple sessions or tokens at once. Behind the scenes, the system checks that requests come from the official site (origin checks) and clearly separates web logins from long-lived API tokens so each kind is managed correctly.

ai.summary: Removed custom CSRF checks and Bearer token validation from `web/src/app/api/api-keys/route.ts`. GET and POST handlers now rely exclusively on `getServerSession` for authentication. This standardizes the auth flow and reduces attack surface by eliminating manual origin checks and direct session table queries.

eli5.text: You no longer need to send a special secret token or worry about where your request comes from just to manage your API keys. If you're signing in normally on the website, that's all that's checked now, the system trusts your login session to prove who you are, nothing extra required. Behind the scenes, the app cleaned up some old verification steps that were doing the same job twice, leaving just one clear path to confirm your identity.

eli5.text: A behind-the-scenes security check on the part of the app that logs you out of your account sessions has been simplified. Previously, there was a custom check meant to block logout requests coming from other websites, but it was removed so the app now relies solely on its standard built-in session verification method. This only affects the action of ending your active sessions; the app will now use one consistent way to confirm your identity across similar features. If you tried to log out of your sessions, the process works the same, just with a slightly leaner codebase behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add graceful shutdown for eval processes
ai.summary: Signal handlers for SIGINT and SIGTERM added to eval runners. Ctrl-C now triggers terminateAllEvalChildren to kill child processes. Covers run-eval-set.ts, run-git-evals.ts, and run-single-eval-process.ts. Windows uses taskkill /T, POSIX uses process.kill(-pid).

eli5.text: When you interrupt an evaluation run by pressing Ctrl-C or asking another program to stop it, the system now stops the entire group of helper processes at once instead of leaving some running. Each helper is told to finish up and exit, and the main coordinator waits for that to happen before the whole run shuts down. This behavior is in place now and affects anyone starting evaluation runs through the tooling. If you look at a run that was being interrupted, you'd see it log that it received the stop request, report how many processes it was terminating, and then exit cleanly rather than stalling or leaving background work behind.

If you look, the step-execution path no longer passes the full private agent state through, and message contents support text-and-image blocks. Nothing visible changes yet for someone just chatting, but it sets up multimodal step generators and safer state passing for future agent work.

ai.title: Refactor base2 orchestration and editor output handling
ai.summary: Updated base2 agent prompts to enforce upfront information gathering, reducing redundant agent spawning. Modified editor agent to mandate `set_output` tool usage for final summaries, injecting `PLACEHOLDER.KNOWLEDGE_FILES_CONTENTS` into the system prompt. Logic now extracts structured `output` from agent state instead of parsing the last assistant message content. Changes confined to `.agents/base2/base2-factory.ts` and `.agents/base2/editor.ts`.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that helps write code now tries to ask every sub-assistant for all the information it will need during a single meeting, instead of having to pull each one back in for follow-up questions. When that assistant finishes its work, it must now place its final explanation into a special output field rather than tacking it onto the end of its reply, so the system can read the summary reliably instead of guessing which line is the conclusion. These tweaks are already live, but they only affect how the internal assistants coordinate behind the scenes; you won't notice any difference in the code they ultimately hand back to you.

ai.title: Server shutdown grace period 5 to 30 min
ai.summary: backend/src/index.ts SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_MS constant 30 * 60 * 1000 replaces hard-coded 300000 timeout. handleShutdown async, awaits Promise before process.exit(1). SIGTERM/SIGINT backend only.

eli5.text: When the server needs to shut down for maintenance or updates, it now gives connected apps and services up to 30 minutes to wrap up their work before turning off completely. Previously, this waiting period was only 5 minutes, so anything still processing when that timer ran out was simply cut off. The team also made the shutdown steps run in the proper order, so the server confirms pending requests are handled before it fully exits. This only affects the backend services, not the apps or websites built on top of them.
